recognize_zh: 視野中央的嗜中性球核分成約 5–6 葉，各葉以細絲相連、染色質粗濃，細胞大小與正常嗜中性球相近；只要出現 ≥6 葉或 ≥5 葉比例增加，即為分葉過多（hypersegmentation）。
features: Single mature neutrophil of normal size
Nucleus with about 5-6 discrete lobes connected by thin chromatin filaments
Pale pink cytoplasm with fine neutrophilic granules; no Döhle bodies or vacuoles evident
Background red cells largely normocytic with scattered platelets
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows a mature neutrophil of normal size with a nucleus divided into approximately five to six lobes joined by thin chromatin filaments. The cytoplasm contains fine neutrophilic granules without obvious toxic granulation or vacuolization. Red cells appear largely normocytic without obvious macro-ovalocytes in this field, and platelets are present. Findings show neutrophil hypersegmentation; correlation with vitamin B12 and folate levels and a differential count of lobe numbers is recommended.

ddx.vs: Megaloblastic anemia shows hypersegmented neutrophils together with macro-ovalocytes and often pancytopenia, which are not evident in this field.
The hereditary form is a benign autosomal dominant trait with hypersegmentation in most neutrophils and normal vitamin levels, requiring family studies.
Morphology is identical, so medication history is required to separate drug-induced hypersegmentation.

ddx.dx: Overlapping bands or two superimposed neutrophils
ddx.vs: Superimposed cells show two separate cytoplasmic outlines, whereas a hypersegmented neutrophil has all lobes within one cytoplasm.
